subject: Post-call: Commercial path & marketplace gating — procurement readiness checklist
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Matthews <jmatthews@cloudspire.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-05-14T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call: Commercial path & marketplace gating — procurement readiness checklist

Hi Jordan — great to meet you and Priya on today’s call. Quick recap and suggested next steps so we can keep momentum on procurement: 

Key notes from the call:
- CloudSpire prefers central finance approval and will likely route through a PO (vs company card).
- Team asked about AWS marketplace private offers vs direct PO billing.
- Procurement will need SOC 2, vendor form, and a high-level billing flow to preview internal approvals.

Proposed next steps (actions & owners):
1) Procurement packet: I’m attaching a short checklist (redwood-procurement-checklist.xlsx) with the items procurement typically asks for. Could you confirm the primary procurement contact and billing address? (Jordan)
2) Marketplace routing: Redwood supports AWS Marketplace Private Offers and direct PO to our AR team. Marissa will share a one-pager on marketplace vs direct PO differences. (Marissa)
3) Contract ops: We can accept a PO and sign a standard MSA; if you want a private offer via AWS, that typically requires a PO + PO number mapping in AWS terms. Monica will coordinate contract & DocuSign steps. (Monica)
4) Timeline check: if procurement can share estimated approval lead-time, we’ll align pricing validity on the quote.

Attachments: initial-quote-CloudSpire-0528.pdf (quote), redwood-procurement-checklist.xlsx

Please flag any items I missed. Happy to jump on a 15-min follow-up with procurement if that speeds things up.

Cheers,
Jonas Weber
Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
jonas_weber@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0126

Date: 2028-05-14T11:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: Commercial path & marketplace gating — procurement readiness checklist

Thanks Jonas — useful summary. Quick answers from our side: 

- Procurement lead is Priya Shah (cc’d). Billing will route through central finance and we expect to use a PO for initial purchase.
- We are interested in the AWS Private Offer route because it helps map costs to specific AWS accounts, but we need to understand if Redwood requires any additional setup on our side.
- Attached our internal procurement policy for reference (cloudspire-procurement-policy.pdf). It calls out standard insurance and security requirements — SOC 2 report access will be required.

Tentative timeline: procurement review next week; approval window ~7-10 business days after we submit the vendor packet. Please send the marketplace one-pager and the vendor form we should complete.

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Matthews <jmatthews@cloudspire.io>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@cloudspire.io>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-05-15T08:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: Commercial path & marketplace gating — procurement readiness checklist

Hi Jordan / Priya — thanks for the quick reply and the procurement policy. Attaching our marketplace pathways one-pager (cloud-marketplace-paths-one-pager.docx) and the vendor intake form we typically use. High-level clarifications below so you can share with procurement: 

Marketplace vs Direct PO (short):
- AWS Private Offer: requires coordination between your AWS account admin and our marketplace team; you still submit a PO to finalize commercial terms, but billing flows via Marketplace. Pros: easier AWS cost allocation, consolidated invoices. Cons: setup takes slightly longer (2–5 business days once terms are agreed).
- Direct PO to Redwood: you issue PO to Redwood AR email; standard net-30 or negotiated terms. Pros: fastest to invoice & collect, simpler onboarding. Cons: no automatic AWS account charge mapping.

Security/compliance: we can provide SOC 2 Type II report and the vendor intake fields in the attached checklist. For SSO/SCIM we support SAML and OIDC — technical contact for SSO proof-of-concept is Jonas.

Requested items from CloudSpire procurement to move forward:
- Completed vendor intake form (attached)
- Copy of anticipated PO template or standard PO language (if you require specific clauses)
- Billing contact and billing address for the PO

If a Private Offer is preferred, please confirm and we’ll loop in our marketplace enablement contact to kick off the AWS steps. Otherwise, if PO is preferred and timing is tight, we can accept PO directly and start onboarding.

Thanks — I’ll follow up with Monica to prepare the MSA and DocuSign link once you confirm path.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>

Date: 2028-05-16T15:04:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Post-call: Commercial path & marketplace gating — procurement readiness checklist

Looping the finance & contract owners to keep things moving. Summary / internal asks: 

1) CloudSpire confirmed PO preference with interest in AWS Private Offer as optional path. Procurement lead: Priya Shah.
2) Karthik — please prepare a billing note: (a) if CloudSpire goes Private Offer, outline fields we need to map (AWS PO number mapping), (b) if direct PO, provide our AR email and standard net terms. Put this in a short email we can forward to Priya.
3) Monica — ready the MSA + standard SOW template and a DocuSign envelope. Use the initial quote attached (initial-quote-CloudSpire-0528.pdf) as basis; set quote validity to 21 days.
4) Marissa — once Karthik has the billing note, please send to Priya with the vendor intake form and marketplace one-pager.

I’m happy to run a 20-min call with Priya and Karthik if procurement prefers synchronous walkthrough.

Attachments referenced: redwood-procurement-checklist.xlsx, cloud-marketplace-paths-one-pager.docx, initial-quote-CloudSpire-0528.pdf

Jonas
